transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... we had this staff meeting at work, and I just got really worked up. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the middle of it, dragging chairs around and waving my arms all over the place to show them how to do it. And I just couldn't seem to stop, even when folks kept telling me to sit down. 

But honestly, those chairs they have in the break room are terrible anyway. They got these little metal legs that scrape up the linoleum if you don't lift them right. My supervisor bought tennis balls to put on the bottom of them once, like you see on the seniors' walkers, you know? But the therapy dogs at the facility kept trying to chew them off. We had this golden retriever visiting on Tuesdays, real sweet dog, but he would just go straight for the tennis balls and get drool all over the floor, which is exactly how people slip in the first place. You ever try to get dog drool out of a floor buffer? It's a nightmare. 

Anyway... yeah, my boss said I had to come see you after the whole chair thing at the meeting.
Can you tell me if you’ve felt unusually energized, hyperactive, or like your thoughts were racing around in your head during that time at work?

Energized? Yeah, I guess you could say that. It's more like... my mind just jumps around constantly. It goes from my job, to church, to my wife, to these new workshop ideas I've got, and it's going so fast that I actually lose the first thought before I can even say it right out loud. 

Like with the workshop ideas, I was thinking about building these elevated planter boxes for the seniors at the facility so they don't have to bend over to garden. Bending over is terrible for the lumbar spine. I saw that in this old training video we had to watch when I first got hired. It was on a VHS tape, if you can believe they still use those. The tracking was all messed up, kept getting those fuzzy white lines across the bottom of the TV screen. My wife actually tried to fix our old VCR at home with a butter knife once. Completely ruined the tape deck. She’s not great with tools, bless her, but she makes a really good meatloaf. Puts a little brown sugar in the ketchup glaze, which sounds weird but it really works. 

But, uh... wait, what did you ask me? Something about my head at work? Yeah, it just spins like that all day long.
During times when your mind is racing and you feel more energetic, do you also notice that your mood is unusually high, irritable, or excited?

Yeah, I guess my mood gets pretty high. There are these stretches where I just feel so bright and fired up, you know? Like everything is finally lining up perfectly and I can take on the world. But then, if someone tries to slow me down or questions what I'm doing, I just snap. Like, way harder than I mean to. 

It's kind of like this one time at the hardware store. I was trying to buy lumber for those planter boxes I mentioned, and the guy working the saw was moving so slow. Just dragging his feet. And he was wearing these thick leather gloves that looked like they hadn't been washed since the nineties. You know the kind, yellow but stained black all over? My uncle used to wear gloves like that when he worked on his old Chevy Nova. Beautiful car, cherry red. He used to let me sit in the driver's seat and pretend to steer when I was a kid. The vinyl seats would get so hot in the summer, though, they'd practically burn the back of your legs if you were wearing shorts. 

Anyway, the guy at the store was taking forever, and I just lost it on him. Started yelling about how he was ruining my whole schedule. I felt bad about it later, but in the moment, it just felt like he was standing in the way of this huge, important thing I had to do.
Have there been times when your mood was so high or you felt so full of energy that it was noticeably different from how you usually feel, and did those times last for at least a week or more?

A week? Oh, yeah, for sure. Way longer than that. These stretches of just being way too energized, you know, where I'm sleeping very little and pushing all these big plans... they've been coming and going for about 11 months now. 

I know it's been exactly that long because it started right around last Thanksgiving. I remember I was up for three days straight trying to build a custom rig to deep-fry the turkey. Because the stands they sell at the store are just complete garbage, right? Cheap aluminum. You drop a twenty-pound bird in the hot oil and the whole thing just wobbles. My buddy Dave actually tipped one over on his driveway a few years back. The grease fire was incredible, just this massive wall of flames. It melted the front bumper right off his wife's Honda Civic. Man, she was furious. She made him sleep out in the garage for a week. 

Which, honestly, isn't even a punishment because Dave's got this great setup out there. He insulated the drywall himself, got a little space heater, and this old corduroy recliner he found at a garage sale. He actually found a silver dollar stuffed down in the cushions of that thing once. Can you imagine? Just sitting there since probably 1972. 

But, uh... yeah, to answer your question, those energetic stretches have been happening on and off for about 11 months.
Have you had any recent periods where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, lasting for several days or more?

Down? Hopeless? No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really get like that, where I'm just sitting around doing nothing. I mean, there's too much to do, right? 

Like, even when I'm not working at the facility, I've got my hands full. Just the other day, I was trying to reorganize the garage because my wife said it was getting too cluttered. And she's right, it is. But that's because I save things that are still good. Like coffee cans. You can use those for so many things. Nails, screws, old drill bits. My granddad used to have his whole basement lined with Folgers cans. Hundreds of them, all labeled with this little label maker he got from Sears. Sears used to be the place to go, you know? You could buy a whole house from their catalog back in the day. A literal house. They'd ship all the lumber and instructions right on a train. It's crazy to think about that now, with Amazon delivering everything in a cardboard box the next day. 

I ordered some new work boots off Amazon last month because the soles on my old ones were totally worn through on the left side. I must drag my left foot a little when I walk. Probably from that time I twisted my ankle playing softball in my twenties. We had this league sponsored by a local pizza joint, and if we won, we got free garlic knots. Best garlic knots in town, hands down. They put this real heavy parmesan on them, not the cheap powdered stuff. 

But no, I don't really get down or lose interest in stuff. If anything, I'm just always trying to keep moving.
